Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{2}{64 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "785a58d5-601a-50af-b1f2-100d273d37ef" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=8 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=8,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{8})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{2}{64 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2\int \frac{1}{1+(8 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2(\frac{1}{8})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(8 x \right)}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "785a58d5-601a-50af-b1f2-100d273d37ef" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "785a58d5-601a-50af-b1f2-100d273d37ef" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{4}{3 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "540dfc73-65b7-5e01-852a-1098e492d974" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=\sqrt{3} x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\sqrt{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{3 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 4\int \frac{1}{1+(\sqrt{3} x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 4(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{3}}{3}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{3}+C \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\sqrt{3} x \right)}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "540dfc73-65b7-5e01-852a-1098e492d974" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "540dfc73-65b7-5e01-852a-1098e492d974" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{8}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "893a3dea-aca6-502a-8459-3475a2d5f36c" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4(1+(\frac{1}{4})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(2)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{8}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{2})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2(2)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 4 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "893a3dea-aca6-502a-8459-3475a2d5f36c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "893a3dea-aca6-502a-8459-3475a2d5f36c" :question/answer-fields $$
x^{2} + 49=49(1+(\frac{1}{49})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{7}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{7},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(7)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{7}{x^{2} + 49}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{7}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{7})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{7}(7)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{7} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "ee64b443-9b0a-5350-bb7e-817a5e6da986" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "ee64b443-9b0a-5350-bb7e-817a5e6da986" :question/answer-fields $$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{9},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(9)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{x^{2} + 81}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{81}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{9})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{81}(9)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{9}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{9} \right)}}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "dbb54453-224c-5927-8847-fd39bd2a8cdb" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "dbb54453-224c-5927-8847-fd39bd2a8cdb" :question/answer-fields $$"] [:db/add "a3f2cb6b-15b8-5ca3-8303-5a5f3b19e4bd" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9(1+(\frac{1}{9})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(3)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{9}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{3})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 1(3)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 3\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 3 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 3 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "a3f2cb6b-15b8-5ca3-8303-5a5f3b19e4bd" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "a3f2cb6b-15b8-5ca3-8303-5a5f3b19e4bd" :question/answer-fields \begin{aligned}& \int \frac{6}{x^{2} + 36}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{6}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{6})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{6}(6)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{6} \right)}+C\end{aligned}

$$"] [:db/add "0328f6eb-ab94-54f1-a3fa-9db716e7cc30" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 81=81(1+(\frac{1}{81})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{9}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{9},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(9)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{8}{x^{2} + 81}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{8}{81}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{9})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{8}{81}(9)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8}{9}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{9}+C \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{9} \right)}}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "0328f6eb-ab94-54f1-a3fa-9db716e7cc30" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "0328f6eb-ab94-54f1-a3fa-9db716e7cc30" :question/answer-fields $$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(8)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{8}{x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{8}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{8}(8)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{8} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "d91f82e1-a5f1-59df-8ebb-04c941947778" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "d91f82e1-a5f1-59df-8ebb-04c941947778" :question/answer-fields $$"] [:db/add "08182b49-5105-5e47-82b6-061be00c1c00" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
252 x^{2} + 7=7(1+(36)x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{252 x^{2} + 7}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{7}\int \frac{1}{1+(6 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{7}(\frac{1}{6})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2}{21}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{21}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(6 x \right)}}{21}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "08182b49-5105-5e47-82b6-061be00c1c00" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "08182b49-5105-5e47-82b6-061be00c1c00" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{4}{2 x^{2} + 49}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "2dc8364c-3b6b-5d4f-a269-88d33ebce849" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
2 x^{2} + 49=49(1+(\frac{2}{49})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{7},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{2 x^{2} + 49}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{49}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{49}(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{7}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{7}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7} \right)}}{7}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "2dc8364c-3b6b-5d4f-a269-88d33ebce849" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "2dc8364c-3b6b-5d4f-a269-88d33ebce849" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{6}{245 x^{2} + 5}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "e24705b1-315a-5355-bc41-cabb19369d0b" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
245 x^{2} + 5=5(1+(49)x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=7 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=7,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{6}{245 x^{2} + 5}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{5}\int \frac{1}{1+(7 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{5}(\frac{1}{7})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{6}{35}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{6 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{35}+C \\  &= \frac{6 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(7 x \right)}}{35}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "e24705b1-315a-5355-bc41-cabb19369d0b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "e24705b1-315a-5355-bc41-cabb19369d0b" :question/answer-fields \int \frac{7}{5 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "55e18530-4dec-572d-a88b-ac0dc3c3ec5b" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
5 x^{2} + 25=25(1+(\frac{1}{5})x^{2})
$$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{5})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{7}{5 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{7}{25}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{5})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{7}{25}(\sqrt{5})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{5}}{25}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{5} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{25}+C \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{5} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{5} \right)}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "55e18530-4dec-572d-a88b-ac0dc3c3ec5b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "55e18530-4dec-572d-a88b-ac0dc3c3ec5b" :question/answer-fields Use the linear substitution $u=2 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{8 x^{2} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+(2 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(2 x \right)}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "f85c1197-a16c-562c-8e6f-5ec36344ebe3" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "f85c1197-a16c-562c-8e6f-5ec36344ebe3" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{5}{7 x^{2} + 36}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "e89cba94-0b9c-53a6-bd8e-752f93d9ffc2" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
7 x^{2} + 36=36(1+(\frac{7}{36})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{6 \sqrt{7}}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{5}{7 x^{2} + 36}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{5}{36}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{5}{36}(\frac{6 \sqrt{7}}{7})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{42}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{42}+C \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6} \right)}}{42}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "e89cba94-0b9c-53a6-bd8e-752f93d9ffc2" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "e89cba94-0b9c-53a6-bd8e-752f93d9ffc2" :question/answer-fields $$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=8,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{8})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{2}{64 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2\int \frac{1}{1+(8 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2(\frac{1}{8})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(8 x \right)}}{4}+C\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{8}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{2})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2(2)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 4 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] ["893a3dea-aca6-502a-8459-3475a2d5f36c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["893a3dea-aca6-502a-8459-3475a2d5f36c" :question/answer-fields "4f5bcf49-2519-5a78-82d8-d2a7e774ebe6"] $$
x^{2} + 36=36(1+(\frac{1}{36})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(6)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{6}{x^{2} + 36}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{6}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{6})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{6}(6)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{6} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] ["da5029da-63e2-508a-a4ed-eaf480260df3" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["da5029da-63e2-508a-a4ed-eaf480260df3" :question/answer-fields "28f53a1f-aec7-56ce-a32a-047c289dbea1"] {:db/id 17592186064219 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186064091 :question/id #uuid "3e89a278-54ab-59a6-adb6-38f43c0fbe9a" :question/math-academy-id "e-471" :question/problem "Calculate the integral  $$
\displaystyle{\int \dfrac{3}{2 + 50x^2} \, \textrm{d}x }.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
\int \dfrac{3}{2 + 50x^2} \, \textrm{d}x = \int \dfrac{3}{2(1 + 25x^2)} = \dfrac 3 2 \int \dfrac{1}{1+25x^2}\,\textrm d x.
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^2}\textrm{d}u =\arctan u +C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u^2$ as the variable, we have $25x^2 = (5x)^2.$

So, let's substitute $u=5x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=5\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac 1 5\,\textrm d u = \textrm d x.
$$

We can now write the integral in terms of $u,$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{2+50{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+25{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+(5x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\,\,\cdot \frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡5x+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "227abe29-6e31-5afd-b0ca-3b8ed7d8c287" :knowledge-point/question-generator {:db/id 17592186492204 :question-generator/id #uuid "45fa7d3a-590c-52a1-b10a-049d979b27b5" :question-generator/script "generate/scratch/17592186064219.py"} :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186064874 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "3b3f469d-d785-54c0-8500-e4f4c541c311" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "6\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)+C" :db/id 17592186330478} {:answer/id #uuid "44fe7e54-fa6e-59d5-8a26-f4f36bb5501f" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)}{3}+C" :db/id 17592186330572} {:answer/id #uuid "848d8e79-5f9b-50c9-a7a2-c023a98ccebf" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "2\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(3x)+C" :db/id 17592186331128} {:answer/id #uuid "be85cd80-7bd6-5b67-8980-2e785a3889ed" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)+C" :db/id 17592186331634} {:answer/id #uuid "fb4584df-c775-5f4a-a59c-6d2f35a59525" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(3x)}{3}+C" :db/id 17592186332157}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "be85cd80-7bd6-5b67-8980-2e785a3889ed" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)+C" :db/id 17592186331634} :answer-field/id #uuid "3e5cefbe-1794-5312-8f1f-f28eb36bbc55" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186332307}] :question/difficulty {:db/ident :question.difficulty/easy} :question/id #uuid "5ff7c3e1-6732-5fb3-bcd2-7ed1aeab0712" :question/math-academy-id "q-49540" :question/problem "$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{2}{64 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=8 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=8,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{8})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{2}{64 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2\int \frac{1}{1+(8 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2(\frac{1}{8})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arctan}{\left(8 x \right)}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{8}{x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 64=64(1+(\frac{1}{64})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(8)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{8}{x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{8}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{8}(8)\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{x}{8} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\int \frac{4}{252 x^{2} + 7}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
252 x^{2} + 7=7(1+(36)x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{252 x^{2} + 7}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{7}\int \frac{1}{1+(6 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{7}(\frac{1}{6})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2}{21}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{21}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(6 x \right)}}{21}+C\end{aligned}
